title: Tool-Bridge: output stability, resume semantics, and error-handling acceptance
creator: Aisha Malik
description: This ticket captures acceptance criteria for the new 'tool-bridge' behavior: a deterministic, resumable layer between streamed structured-model emissions and downstream tool/function invocations. Focus is on clear framing/metadata, idempotent resume, observable error classification, and safe fallbacks when tool calls fail or partial JSON is emitted. Deliverables: acceptance criteria list, example payloads, minimal protocol handshake, and integration notes for Console telemetry and SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: Schema handshake header: Every streaming session MUST start with a single JSON metadata frame with keys: protocol_version (string), schema_id (string), schema_version (string), request_id (string), and optional resume_token_support (boolean-as-string). Clients must be able to reject a stream if protocol_version or schema_id are incompatible.

Framing and boundaries: Streamed structured output MUST use newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) frames where each application-frame contains either 'emit' or 'checkpoint' in a top-level 'frame_type' field. Parsers must ignore unknown additional fields safely.

Checkpoint semantics: A 'checkpoint' frame commits all prior 'emit' frames as durable for downstream tooling. Checkpoints include monotonically increasing checkpoint_index (stringified integer) and an optional resume_token (opaque string). Resume behavior MUST use the latest checkpoint_index and resume_token to avoid reprocessing already-committed tool calls.

Resume and idempotency: When a client reconnects with a resume_token, the platform MUST ensure any tool invocations already acknowledged by a checkpoint are not re-invoked. Tool calls initiated but not checkpoint-acknowledged can be replayed but must be marked with an idempotency_key header derived from request_id + emit_index.

Tool call invocation model: The bridge supports two flavors: inline (synchronous: function call result is embedded as an 'emit' with tool_result metadata) and async (out-of-band: bridge emits a 'tool_request' frame with request_id and waits for 'tool_response' later). Acceptance requires deterministic routing: inline calls must not exceed configured inline_time_budget; if budget exceeded, bridge must downgrade to async and emit a 'downgrade_notice' frame.

Error classification and fallback policy: Tool-level failures must map to one of: transient (retryable with backoff), permanent (do not retry), partial-success (return available partial payload). The bridge MUST emit a 'tool_status' frame with 'status_code' (string), 'classification' (one of transient|permanent|partial), and human-readable 'message'. For high-severity permanent failures where the tool is critical, the stream SHOULD include an explicit 'graceful_fallback' emit indicating the alternate action (fallback_model_id or alternative_steps).

Partial JSON and recovery: If the model produces incomplete or malformed JSON for an 'emit' that is necessary for a tool call, the bridge MUST attempt a single automatic normalization pass (heuristic fixes) and, if still invalid, mark the emit as 'malformed' and attach a parse_error frame with a short snippet and suggested correction. Such emits must not be checkpointed until corrected or explicitly marked to proceed by the client.

Telemetry and observability hooks: Each frame MUST include minimal telemetry context fields: request_id, emit_index, model_variant, and region. Console must surface per-request timeline events (first-emit, first-tool-call, checkpoint, downgrade, resume). Acceptance requires a sample dashboard tile showing average time-between-emit-and-tool-response and resume success rate.

Backpressure and batching: The bridge MUST support an optional emit_batching window (configurable) that groups multiple emits targeting the same tool into a single tooling request when safe. Batching decisions and final batch size must be exposed in telemetry frames. If batching introduces latency beyond client SLO, downgrade to single-call behavior.

Security: Tool requests that include PII or secrets must be flagged by the 'sensitivity' field (low|medium|high). High sensitivity flows MUST route through encrypted private deployment paths (if the customer's environment requires) and must never be logged in plain text in telemetry; Console sample traces should show redacted placeholders.

SDK compatibility: JavaScript and Python SDKs MUST provide a convenience 'resume_stream' API that accepts resume_token and transparently reconciles checkpoint_index. The SDK must expose a 'on_tool_status' callback to surface tool_classification decisions to integrators.

Compatibility and versioning: The bridge must reject streams where protocol_version major component differs (e.g., '1.x' vs '2.x'); minor differences are allowed with best-effort parsing and a warning frame. Acceptance requires unit tests for both 'major mismatch' rejection and a backward-compatible minor upgrade scenario.

Documentation and examples: Include three example end-to-end traces: (1) inline tool success with checkpoint, (2) async tool request with resume after transient tool outage, (3) malformed emit corrected by heuristic normalization then checkpointed. Examples must include raw NDJSON frames and instructions for SDK integration.

Failure-mode runbook: The PRD must include an operational runbook for: stuck-resume (token mismatch), double-invoke detection, and checkpoint lag. Each runbook step must map to a Console action or API call and include expected telemetry signals to look for.

Performance SLOs: For inline tool calls the 95th percentile end-to-end latency (emit→tool_result) must be < 350ms under normal load in hosted tier; for async calls the platform must deliver a tool_response frame within 99th percentile 2s under normal load. Acceptance requires synthetic load validation results attached to this ticket.

Privacy and audit: All tool invocations must surface an audit_event frame that contains actor_id, tool_name, and timestamp. These frames must be indexable in the customer's audit logs; acceptance requires a sample of stored audit entries demonstrating searchability by actor_id and request_id.
notes: Related PM tickets: PM-19876 (incremental-typed-frames), PM-50882 (function-calling-observability) — these are referenced for telemetry overlap but this ticket avoids duplicating streaming contract language.
